# 03 — Planets & Voxel Scale

Every planet in EXODUS PROTOCOL is a **voxel planet at traversal scale: 20–120 km in diameter**, starting with the starter planet, a 120 km gameplay-scale Earth. At this scale a planet is huge on foot or by rover and has a crust deep enough for extensive voxel mining, without thousands of kilometres of empty terrain. Curvature is visible from orbit, but the surface feels flat when you're standing on it.



## The voxel planet standard

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Diameter | 20–120 km (Earth is the maximum) |
| Construction | Cube-sphere: six cube-face heightmaps plus biome, ore and Bloom maps drive voxel generation; hand-authored regions are stamped on top |
| Voxel resolution | 1.0 m voxels in 32 m chunks, 8 clipmap LOD rings |
| Terrain elevation | ±3.5% of radius |
| Minable crust | 3.5% of radius, then unminable bedrock |
| Atmosphere height | 15% of radius (atmospheric thrusters fade to zero at the top) |
| Gravity | Gameplay value per planet (0.1–1.8 g). Full strength up to the tallest terrain, then falls off as (R/r)^7; zero beyond 2 R |
| Hand-authored regions | Built flat in a local east-north-up frame, up to 16 × 16 km and no more than 25% of the planet's diameter, then stamped onto the cube-face heightmaps (the stamp absorbs the curvature drop) |
| Cube-face heightmaps | 2,048² (20 km) · 4,096² (40 km) · 8,192² (80–120 km), 16-bit |

## Why curvature matters to level design

On a small planet the horizon is close. Landmarks must be tall enough to clear it, or navigation breaks. Required landmark height = (distance − horizon)² / (2 × radius).

| Diameter | Horizon at 1.8 m | Landmark height to be seen from 500 m | 1 km | 2 km | 5 km | Drop over 8 km |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 km | 190 m | 5 m | 33 m | 164 m | 1,157 m | 800 m |
| 40 km | 268 m | 1 m | 13 m | 75 m | 560 m | 400 m |
| 60 km | 329 m | ground | 8 m | 47 m | 364 m | 267 m |
| 80 km | 379 m | ground | 5 m | 33 m | 267 m | 200 m |
| 100 km | 424 m | ground | 3 m | 25 m | 209 m | 160 m |
| 120 km | 465 m | ground | 2 m | 20 m | 171 m | 133 m |

**Rules that follow:**
1. Every district's primary landmark must be tall enough to be seen from 2 km on its planet (Earth: 20 m or more; the Moon: 75 m or more).
2. Place landmarks on high ground: every 10 m of elevation adds about as much reach as 10 m of height.
3. Flat regions are capped at 16 km on a side and at a quarter of the planet's diameter (10 km on the Moon, 5 km on a 20 km planet), so stamping error stays small; bigger areas are split into several stamps.
4. Author the horizon: hills and mesas should hide the close geometric horizon so the world feels bigger than it is.

## Solar-system scale

| Route | Distance | Travel |
|---|---|---|
| Earth surface → Haven-9 (LEO) | 25 km altitude | About 1 min: launch, atmosphere exit, short space hop (pulse is blocked this close to Earth) |
| Earth → Moon | 360 km centre to centre | About 30 s by pulse drive, plus the Moon's approach |
| Earth → Styx Wreck | 1,500 km | About 1 min by pulse drive (needs extended range and radiation shielding, M2.07) |
| Planet → planet in a Drift system | 800–4,000 km | Pulse drive, 45 s – 2.5 min (may be interrupted by encounters) |
| System → system | Sower jump lane | Jump: 10 s charge + 8–12 s jump tunnel, 5 min cooldown |

- **Kits:** [KIT-DST](10-modular-kits.md#kit-dst--desert-terrain-dressing), [KIT-JUN](10-modular-kits.md#kit-jun--veyra-jungle), [KIT-ICE](10-modular-kits.md#kit-ice--ice-caves--cathedral), [KIT-BLM](10-modular-kits.md#kit-blm--bloom-overlay)
